title: Fix runner recovery commits failing on pre-commit hooks and crash-looping
goal:
## Problem
In runner/project.js, both worktree recovery-branch commits run `git commit` without `--no-verify`:
- Reused worktree recovery: `recovery: unpushed work from reused worktree (<branch>)` (runner/project.js ~line 665)
- Eviction recovery: `recovery: unpushed work parked before eviction (<dir>)` (runner/project.js ~line 369)

Because these commits are purely local safety snapshots on `kb-recovery/*` branches meant to preserve unpushed residue before resetting a worktree, any failing repo `pre-commit` hook (such as `binary-guard` rejecting corrupt PNGs, or linter/formatter hooks) aborts the commit. The uncaught error crashes the runner process (exit code 1), causing systemd to restart it in an infinite loop (observed: 10,776 restarts on local-alpha for kb-7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21) and blocking the runner from picking up other tasks.

## Goal
1. Pass `--no-verify` when creating internal `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits in runner/project.js (both reuse and eviction paths) so repo pre-commit hooks cannot block parking unpushed work.
2. Ensure errors during worktree setup/recovery in the runner daemon are caught per-task (failing/releasing the task cleanly rather than crashing the runner process into a restart loop).
3. Add regression tests in runner/project.test.js verifying that dirty worktrees with a failing pre-commit hook still park cleanly onto `kb-recovery/*` during both reuse and eviction.
body:
## Problem
In runner/project.js, both worktree recovery-branch commits run `git commit` without `--no-verify`:
- Reused worktree recovery: `recovery: unpushed work from reused worktree (<branch>)` (runner/project.js ~line 665)
- Eviction recovery: `recovery: unpushed work parked before eviction (<dir>)` (runner/project.js ~line 369)

Because these commits are purely local safety snapshots on `kb-recovery/*` branches meant to preserve unpushed residue before resetting a worktree, any failing repo `pre-commit` hook (such as `binary-guard` rejecting corrupt PNGs, or linter/formatter hooks) aborts the commit. The uncaught error crashes the runner process (exit code 1), causing systemd to restart it in an infinite loop (observed: 10,776 restarts on local-alpha for kb-7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21) and blocking the runner from picking up other tasks.

## Goal
1. Pass `--no-verify` when creating internal `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits in runner/project.js (both reuse and eviction paths) so repo pre-commit hooks cannot block parking unpushed work.
2. Ensure errors during worktree setup/recovery in the runner daemon are caught per-task (failing/releasing the task cleanly rather than crashing the runner process into a restart loop).
3. Add regression tests in runner/project.test.js verifying that dirty worktrees with a failing pre-commit hook still park cleanly onto `kb-recovery/*` during both reuse and eviction.

1|# Stage Review — `--no-verify` recovery snapshots + per-task daemon containment
2|
3|Reviewer: PR-review stage (docs-only). Reviewed the branch diff vs `main` and ran the
4|suites. Verdict: PASS (see final verdict block in the stage output).
5|
6|## What changed (diff vs main)
7|
8|- `runner/project.js` — new shared helper `commitRecoverySnapshot(workdir, message, { recoveryBranch, log })`
9|  owning the recovery-commit argv: repo-local identity + `commit --no-verify -m <message>`,
10|  a warn log naming the recovery branch and the bypass, and a fail-safe "nothing staged" skip.
11|  Both call sites now use it:
12|  - `preserveEvictedWorkdir` (eviction): `recovery: unpushed work parked before eviction (<dir>)`
13|  - `refreshWorktreeToRemote` (reuse): `recovery: unpushed work from reused worktree (<branch>)`
14|- `runner/daemon.js` — `runDispatchLoop` wraps `await executeAssignment(...)` in try/catch:
15|  `STALE_EPOCH` rethrows (fencing must propagate); any other error is logged
16|  (`logger.error`/`warn`/`console.error`, each guarded) and the loop continues to the
17|  reap + self-update + next poll. `executeAssignment` still rethrows, so
18|  `runSingleAssignment` keeps its non-zero-exit contract.
19|- `runner/project.test.js` — `installFailingHook` fixture (always-fail `pre-commit` via
20|  `core.hooksPath`, with a probe commit proving it fires) plus:
21|  - reuse path parks past a failing hook (`recoveredTo` matches `^kb-recovery/t1/`, file in
22|    `git ls-tree`, worktree clean, exact subject)
23|  - eviction path parks past a failing hook (same assertions + task-branch tip unchanged)
24|  - `commitRecoverySnapshot` unit tests: bypasses hooks + warn-logs branch; nothing-staged
25|    skip; blank-input rejection
26|- `runner/daemon.test.js` — loop-containment test: first assignment's project path has no
27|  repo (setup throws), task is interrupt-released, loop logs and serves the next assignment.
28|- `runner/gitOps.test.js` — scope pin: with a failing hook installed, `commitAndPush` on a
29|  task branch still rejects and commits nothing (hooks unchanged outside recovery).
30|- `runner/README.md` — documents the recovery-snapshot hook bypass + warn and the
31|  per-task loop containment.
32|
33|## Verification performed this stage
34|
35|| Check | Result |
36||---|---|
37|| `node --test runner/project.test.js` | 41/41 pass |
38|| `node --test runner/daemon.test.js` | 158/158 pass |
39|| `node --test runner/gitOps.test.js` | 11/11 pass |
40|| Full runner suite (README gate command, 19 files) | 449/449 pass |
41|| Red→green, recovery tests: scratch copy with `--no-verify` removed | 3 new hook tests FAIL (38 pass / 3 fail) — tests are real regression tests |
42|| Red→green, daemon test: scratch copy with loop catch reverse-applied | new containment test FAILS (157/158) — catch is load-bearing |
43|| Scope: `grep -- "--no-verify" runner/` (non-test) | only `runner/project.js:454` inside the helper |
44|| `kb-recovery` commit creation sites | only the two paths in `project.js`, both via the helper |
45|| `executeAssignment` rethrow | intact (daemon.js:2373), `runSingleAssignment` contract preserved |
46|| Post-catch flow | reap + self-update still run after a contained failure (daemon.js:3028+) |
47|
48|## Review questions
49|
50|- **Achieves the goal?** Yes. Both `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits (reuse ~line 840 and
51|  eviction ~line 518 in project.js) go through one helper that passes `--no-verify`;
52|  the dispatch loop contains per-task failures instead of exiting 1; regression tests
53|  cover both paths with a failing pre-commit hook.
54|- **Followed the plan?** Yes — helper extraction, warn log (survey q3), loop-level catch
55|  keeping `interrupt` routing (survey q2 = re-queue), `STALE_EPOCH` propagation preserved,
56|  `runSingleAssignment` untouched, docs updated. One deliberate deviation: SURVEY q1's
57|  selected answer was "skip checks for all automatic runner saves", but the task goal and
58|  the plan's non-goals scope the bypass to `kb-recovery/*` only; the new gitOps test pins
59|  that task-branch commits still run hooks. The task goal text is authoritative here, so
60|  the implementation is correct as scoped.
61|- **Code standards / tech debt?** The helper removes duplication rather than adding it;
62|  the "nothing staged" fail-safe is narrowly matched (`git-failed` + /nothing to commit/i)
63|  so real git errors still throw. No new dependencies, config, or wire changes. The catch
64|  block guards every logging sink so the barrier itself cannot throw.
65|- **Maintainability?** Single home for recovery-commit argv prevents drift between the
66|  reuse and eviction paths; warn log keeps the bypass discoverable.
67|- **Docs?** `runner/README.md` recovery/loop section updated; JSDoc on touched functions
68|  updated. No other docs reference the old behavior.
69|

73|  (runner survives; task flaps) — same shape as the existing `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`
74|  handling; backoff is out of scope per the plan.
75|- Bypassed snapshots can park corrupt binaries by design; the warn log names the branch.

1|# Implementation Plan — `--no-verify` for `kb-recovery/*` snapshots + per-task daemon containment
2|
3|Task: `db49d6c6-bdd5-4600-aaea-15a71042ae20`
4|Source problem: runner `git commit` without `--no-verify` on internal recovery branches; uncaught worktree-setup error crashes the runner into a systemd restart loop.
5|Survey input: [SURVEY.md](./SURVEY.md) (Round 1; `answers: {}` — unanswered, so the recommended options below are carried as assumptions pending confirmation).
6|
7|## Goal
8|
9|1. Internal `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits in `runner/project.js` (both the reuse path and the eviction path) pass `--no-verify`, so repo `pre-commit` hooks (binary-guard, linters, formatters) can never block parking unpushed residue.
10|2. Worktree setup/recovery errors in the runner daemon are contained per-task: the task is failed/released cleanly and the daemon keeps polling instead of exiting 1 into a systemd restart loop.
11|3. Regression tests in `runner/project.test.js` prove dirty worktrees with a failing `pre-commit` hook still park cleanly onto `kb-recovery/*` via both reuse and eviction.
12|
13|## Success Criteria
14|
15|- Both recovery commits (`recovery: unpushed work from reused worktree (…)` in `refreshWorktreeToRemote`, `runner/project.js` ~line 789; `recovery: unpushed work parked before eviction (…)` in `preserveEvictedWorkdir`, `runner/project.js` ~line 466) succeed with a deliberately failing `pre-commit` hook installed, and the parked content is verifiable on the `kb-recovery/*` branch.
16|- A `prepareWorkdir`/recovery throw inside one assignment no longer terminates `runDispatchLoop`: the loop logs, releases the task, and continues to the next poll. No new crash path is introduced for `runSingleAssignment` (single-shot mode must still exit non-zero on failure so callers/CI see it).
17|- `node --test runner/project.test.js runner/daemon.test.js` passes, and the repo's unit gate (`npm test`, which runs the `runner` suite via `scripts/run-tests.mjs`) passes.
18|- Normal (non-recovery) runner commits — e.g. harness wrap-up commits on the task branch — still run hooks unchanged.
19|
20|## Survey decisions (factored in)
21|
22|`SURVEY.md` Round 1 asked three questions; all are unanswered (`"answers": {}`). This plan adopts the recommended option for each as a working assumption (flagged for confirmation in Open Questions):
23|
24|| # | Question | Adopted (recommended) answer | Plan effect |
25||---|----------|------------------------------|-------------|
26|| q1 | Skip checks for emergency backups? | Yes — emergency backups only | `--no-verify` applies ONLY to the two `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits, never to task-branch or integration commits. |
27|| q2 | What to do with the one failed task? | Mark failed, move to next task | Contain per-task and keep polling. Refinement: keep the existing `interrupt` (release/re-queue) routing for generic errors rather than `complete(failed)` — see Key Decision 2 for why. Runner survival is the requirement; routing stays as-is. |
28|| q3 | Visibility of skipped checks? | Clear warning in logs | Emit a `logger.warn` naming the recovery branch and stating hooks were bypassed, at each snapshot commit. |
29|
30|## Approach
31|
32|Follow "make the change easy, then make the change":
33|
34|1. **Easy first:** extract the two near-identical inline recovery-commit blocks into one shared helper (single home for identity flags, message, `--no-verify`, and the warn log), with zero behavior change; add a shared failing-hook test fixture. Land this refactor green before touching behavior.
35|2. **Then the change:** one-line behavior change inside the helper (`--no-verify` + warn log), plus the two regression tests.
36|3. **Then containment:** a loop-level `try/catch` around the `executeAssignment` call in `runDispatchLoop` (the proven crash path — see Evidence), with a daemon test; deliberately NOT by removing the rethrow inside `executeAssignment`, which single-shot mode depends on.
37|
38|No new dependencies, no new config flags, no schema/wire changes.
39|
40|## Evidence (what the research established)
41|
42|- **Commit sites:** `runner/project.js` `preserveEvictedWorkdir` (~line 463–467) and `refreshWorktreeToRemote` (~line 786–790) both run `git commit` with `-c user.name/email` but no `--no-verify`. A hook failure surfaces as `RunnerGitError(code: "git-failed")` via `runGit`.
43|- **Crash path:** `executeAssignment` (`runner/daemon.js` ~line 2243–2333) catches generic errors, best-effort `client.interrupt`s, then **rethrows** (line 2332). `runDispatchLoop` awaits `executeAssignment` (line 2928) with **no `try/catch`**, and the loop body has only `try/finally` — so the throw escapes `runLoop` → `main()` (`runner/main.js`) rejects → process exits 1 → systemd restarts → the interrupted task re-queues and the same poisoned worktree is reclaimed → observed 10,776-restart loop. The `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` precedent (interrupt + return, lines 2246–2262) shows the codebase's own pattern for "infra problem, don't die".
44|- **Hook mechanics:** `scripts/githooks/pre-commit` is the binary guard; `core.hooksPath=scripts/githooks` is set repo-wide and inherited by linked `kb-*` worktrees (existing test at `runner/project.test.js` ~line 364 proves inheritance). So a corrupt PNG staged anywhere in a reused/evicted worktree deterministically aborts both recovery commits today.
45|- **Test patterns to reuse:** `originWithWorktree()` + `refreshWorktreeToRemote` reuse test (~line 73), eviction parking test (~line 525), staged-index regression test (~line 731), `localRepo()` helper (~line 27). New tests mirror these with a failing hook installed.
46|- **Test entrypoints:** focused — `node --test runner/project.test.js`; full unit gate — `npm test` (`scripts/run-tests.mjs`, "Unit Tests (runner)" suite names `runner/*.test.js` explicitly).
47|
48|## Key Decisions
49|
50|1. **Scope of `--no-verify`: recovery snapshots only (survey q1).** These commits are local safety snapshots on `kb-recovery/*`, never pushed as task output and never merged; hook value there is zero and hook cost is a wedged runner. All other runner-authored commits keep hooks. Rejected: `--no-verify` everywhere (loses the binary-guard backstop on real output), and deleting/disabling repo hooks (mutates user repos).
51|2. **Containment via loop-level catch, keeping `interrupt` routing (survey q2, refined).** The minimal correct fix is `try/catch` around `await executeAssignment(...)` in `runDispatchLoop`: log the error, continue polling. The task is already released by the `interrupt` inside `executeAssignment`'s catch, satisfying "failing/releasing the task cleanly". Changing generic errors to `complete(outcome: failed)` instead would newly fail tasks for transient infra blips (network, lock contention) — a behavior change far beyond this task — so routing is left untouched. Rejected: removing the rethrow in `executeAssignment` (breaks `runSingleAssignment`'s non-zero-exit contract and the `STALE_EPOCH` contract).
52|3. **Shared helper over two one-line edits.** Both commit blocks duplicate identity flags and message shape; a `commitRecoverySnapshot(workdir, message, { logger })` helper (name to match repo conventions at implementation time) makes the bypass auditable in one place and prevents future drift between the paths. The helper owns: `-c` identity flags, `--no-verify`, the message, and the q3 warn log.
53|4. **Failing-hook fixture, not the real binary guard, in tests.** Tests install a trivial `#!/bin/sh; exit 1` hook (via `core.hooksPath` on a fixture dir or a `.git/hooks/pre-commit` file in the temp repo) so they are hermetic, fast, and independent of `check-binary-guard.mjs` internals. One test may additionally exercise the real guard with a corrupt PNG if cheap, but it is not required.
54|

Thread the logger through (check how `project.js` logs today; if it has no logger, `console.warn` via an injectable param defaulting to console, matching testability).

Keep the post-assignment reap + self-update flow reachable after a caught error (place the catch so the loop proceeds to the next iteration cleanly; decide at implementation time whether reap should run for the failed assignment — recommended: yes, keep it inline by catching narrowly around `executeAssignment` only).

96||-------|--------------------|----------|

106|## Risks
107|
108|- **Masking real damage (q1 trade-off):** bypassed snapshots can park corrupt binaries. Accepted by design (survey q1): recovery branches are forensic snapshots, and the q3 warn log preserves discoverability. Mitigation: log message includes branch name + reason.
109|- **Poison-task flap:** after containment, a task whose setup fails persistently will interrupt/re-queue and be reclaimed repeatedly (runner survives, task flaps). import { GIT_FAILURE_PARK_AFTER } from "../../../shared/gitFailure.js";

/***
 * MARK: isGitFailureParked
 * @description Whether a task is parked after consecutive deterministic git
 *   failures: its `gitFailureStreak` reached `GIT_FAILURE_PARK_AFTER`
 *   strikes and still names the task's current stage. A stage change (the
 *   failback walk, an operator move) unparks by mismatch — the walk itself
 *   terminates because a stage that keeps failing in place re-parks — while
 *   an operator retry/resume/move or any success clears the streak
 *   outright. Consumed by the single dispatch gate
 *   (`isSchedulerRunnable`) and the direct-claim route, so parked tasks
 *   take no embedded or Runner work until the operator acts. Never throws.
 * @example isGitFailureParked({ currentStageId: 'build', gitFailureStreak: { stageId: 'build', signature: 'hook-rejected|pre-commit|stage-commit|a.png', count: 3 } }) => true
 * @example isGitFailureParked({ currentStageId: 'build' }) => false
 * @param {Object} [task] - Task object, may carry `gitFailureStreak`.
 * @returns {boolean} True when auto-dispatch must skip this task.
 ***/
export function isGitFailureParked(task) {
	if (!task || typeof task !== "object") return false;
	const streak = task.gitFailureStreak;
	if (!streak || typeof streak !== "object" || Array.isArray(streak)) return false;
	if (!Number.isInteger(streak.count) || streak.count < GIT_FAILURE_PARK_AFTER) return false;
	if (typeof streak.stageId !== "string" || !streak.stageId) return false;
	if (typeof streak.signature !== "string" || !streak.signature) return false;
	return streak.stageId === task.currentStageId;
}

=====

# ADR 0017 — Surface runner commit/hook failures in the task UI

**Status:** Accepted.
**Date:** 2026-11-21.
**Context:** Task `1cae113f-43ab-4613-801b-2de6297637fd` — on task
`7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21` the repo pre-commit binary-guard hook
rejected 3 corrupt PNGs during a runner recovery commit. The runner wrote the
error only to its systemd journal, exited 1, and restarted 10,776 times under
`Restart=always`, while the task UI showed status `interrupted` with a stale
`lastError` from an earlier human rejection. Commit/hook failures were
invisible and crash-looped the runner.

## Decision

1. **One shared `GitFailureDetails` contract** (`shared/gitFailure/`): kind
   (`hook-rejected`, `commit-failed`, `merge-conflict`, reserved
   `push-failed`/`auth-failed`), lifecycle phase, failing command, exit code,
   hook name, affected files, hook output, remedy, and one-line summary, with
   transport caps. The runner, backend, and UI share it verbatim — no layer
   invents field names.
2. **The runner classifies hook/commit failures and reports them as failed
   completions, never rethrows.** A deterministic rejection (hook, commit, or
   merge conflict) flows through `complete({ outcome: "failed",
   failureKind: "commit-failed", gitFailure })` and the daemon returns, so
   the process stays alive and systemd never restarts. Transient git faults
   (lock/timeout) keep the interrupt path, now carrying a reason. This
   covers task-branch (stage/merge) commits; internal `kb-recovery/*`
   snapshots bypass hooks instead (see 6).
3. **Complete-not-interrupt is the reporting vehicle.** Only the complete path
   flows through failure routing into `lastError`, timeline, history, logs,
   and the `-failure-` stage report; `interrupt()` deliberately leaves
   `lastError` alone. Worktree-setup failures report the same way — the
   complete fence only checks the claim hold, never progress state.
4. **The backend persists the envelope as `lastError.gitDiagnostics`** (new
   `hook-rejected`/`commit-failed` kinds beside `merge-conflict`/
   `sync-blocked`), classifies `failureKind: "commit-failed"` as
   non-retryable logical feedback, and parks the task after three
   consecutive same-signature strikes (`gitFailureStreak`, scheduler +
   claim skip until an operator retries, resumes, or moves).
5. **The task UI renders a dedicated callout** (hook, command, files, remedy,
   expandable full output) inside both failure banners plus a distinct card
   label — driven by the envelope shape, so backend diagnostics shapes keep
   rendering as plain text.
6. **Scoped bypass for recovery snapshots only; never bypass or auto-repair
   task output.** Internal `kb-recovery/*` snapshots bypass repo hooks via
   `commitRecoverySnapshot` (a failing hook must never strand unpushed work;
   the bypass is warn-logged with the recovery branch). Task-branch
   (stage/merge) commits never bypass — no `--no-verify` there (pinned by a
   scope test), no file deletion, no hook disabling. Parking (stop retrying)
   is the only other automation.

**Reconciliation note (2026-11-21).** This ADR originally forbade all bypass
(q6 survey override). Merged task `db49d6c6` then fixed the same incident's
recovery path with `--no-verify` recovery snapshots, and the recorded human
survey answer for q6 selects `--no-verify` retry — so this branch reconciled
onto that design during the merge with `main` (`64e428e6`): bypass is allowed
exactly inside `commitRecoverySnapshot`, forbidden everywhere else. The
`recovery` envelope phase is retained for wire compatibility but has no
producer. Human confirmation of this q6 middle ground (scoped recovery
bypass, no blanket auto-retry) is requested at merge review.

## Consequences

- Hook rejections become visible, actionable task errors with a concrete fix
  instead of journal-only crash loops; the stale-`lastError` mechanism for
  this class is gone (fresh `failureReason` on every failed completion).
- Same-tree retries are bounded: one poll-cycle backoff on the runner, three
  strikes then scheduler/claim parking on the backend, operator action to
  unpark. No new task status was introduced.
- The envelope doubles as the agent handoff: failback already carries
  `gitDiagnostics` into the Tier-3 prompt, so a follow-up remediation stage
  can consume it without a new channel.

## Follow-ups (deliberately out of scope)

- Push/network/auth classification (reserved kinds, one parser).
- Team webhook on hook failure.
- Agent auto-remediation stage consuming `gitDiagnostics`.

import { GIT_FAILURE_PARK_AFTER } from "../../../shared/gitFailure.js";

/***
 * MARK: isGitFailureParked
 * @description Whether a task is parked after consecutive deterministic git
 *   failures: its `gitFailureStreak` reached `GIT_FAILURE_PARK_AFTER`
 *   strikes and still names the task's current stage. A stage change (the
 *   failback walk, an operator move) unparks by mismatch — the walk itself
 *   terminates because a stage that keeps failing in place re-parks — while
 *   an operator retry/resume/move or any success clears the streak
 *   outright. Consumed by the single dispatch gate
 *   (`isSchedulerRunnable`) and the direct-claim route, so parked tasks
 *   take no embedded or Runner work until the operator acts. Never throws.
 * @example isGitFailureParked({ currentStageId: 'build', gitFailureStreak: { stageId: 'build', signature: 'hook-rejected|pre-commit|stage-commit|a.png', count: 3 } }) => true
 * @example isGitFailureParked({ currentStageId: 'build' }) => false
 * @param {Object} [task] - Task object, may carry `gitFailureStreak`.
 * @returns {boolean} True when auto-dispatch must skip this task.
 ***/
export function isGitFailureParked(task) {
	if (!task || typeof task !== "object") return false;
	const streak = task.gitFailureStreak;
	if (!streak || typeof streak !== "object" || Array.isArray(streak)) return false;
	if (!Number.isInteger(streak.count) || streak.count < GIT_FAILURE_PARK_AFTER) return false;
	if (typeof streak.stageId !== "string" || !streak.stageId) return false;
	if (typeof streak.signature !== "string" || !streak.signature) return false;
	return streak.stageId === task.currentStageId;
}

=====

# ADR 0017 — Surface runner commit/hook failures in the task UI

**Status:** Accepted.
**Date:** 2026-11-21.
**Context:** Task `1cae113f-43ab-4613-801b-2de6297637fd` — on task
`7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21` the repo pre-commit binary-guard hook
rejected 3 corrupt PNGs during a runner recovery commit. The runner wrote the
error only to its systemd journal, exited 1, and restarted 10,776 times under
`Restart=always`, while the task UI showed status `interrupted` with a stale
`lastError` from an earlier human rejection. Commit/hook failures were
invisible and crash-looped the runner.

## Decision

1. **One shared `GitFailureDetails` contract** (`shared/gitFailure/`): kind
   (`hook-rejected`, `commit-failed`, `merge-conflict`, reserved
   `push-failed`/`auth-failed`), lifecycle phase, failing command, exit code,
   hook name, affected files, hook output, remedy, and one-line summary, with
   transport caps. The runner, backend, and UI share it verbatim — no layer
   invents field names.
2. **The runner classifies hook/commit failures and reports them as failed
   completions, never rethrows.** A deterministic rejection (hook, commit, or
   merge conflict) flows through `complete({ outcome: "failed",
   failureKind: "commit-failed", gitFailure })` and the daemon returns, so
   the process stays alive and systemd never restarts. Transient git faults
   (lock/timeout) keep the interrupt path, now carrying a reason. This
   covers task-branch (stage/merge) commits; internal `kb-recovery/*`
   snapshots bypass hooks instead (see 6).
3. **Complete-not-interrupt is the reporting vehicle.** Only the complete path
   flows through failure routing into `lastError`, timeline, history, logs,
   and the `-failure-` stage report; `interrupt()` deliberately leaves
   `lastError` alone. Worktree-setup failures report the same way — the
   complete fence only checks the claim hold, never progress state.
4. **The backend persists the envelope as `lastError.gitDiagnostics`** (new
   `hook-rejected`/`commit-failed` kinds beside `merge-conflict`/
   `sync-blocked`), classifies `failureKind: "commit-failed"` as
   non-retryable logical feedback, and parks the task after three
   consecutive same-signature strikes (`gitFailureStreak`, scheduler +
   claim skip until an operator retries, resumes, or moves).
5. **The task UI renders a dedicated callout** (hook, command, files, remedy,
   expandable full output) inside both failure banners plus a distinct card
   label — driven by the envelope shape, so backend diagnostics shapes keep
   rendering as plain text.
6. **Scoped bypass for recovery snapshots only; never bypass or auto-repair
   task output.** Internal `kb-recovery/*` snapshots bypass repo hooks via
   `commitRecoverySnapshot` (a failing hook must never strand unpushed work;
   the bypass is warn-logged with the recovery branch). Task-branch
   (stage/merge) commits never bypass — no `--no-verify` there (pinned by a
   scope test), no file deletion, no hook disabling. Parking (stop retrying)
   is the only other automation.

**Reconciliation note (2026-11-21).** This ADR originally forbade all bypass
(q6 survey override). Merged task `db49d6c6` then fixed the same incident's
recovery path with `--no-verify` recovery snapshots, and the recorded human
survey answer for q6 selects `--no-verify` retry — so this branch reconciled
onto that design during the merge with `main` (`64e428e6`): bypass is allowed
exactly inside `commitRecoverySnapshot`, forbidden everywhere else. The
`recovery` envelope phase is retained for wire compatibility but has no
producer. Human confirmation of this q6 middle ground (scoped recovery
bypass, no blanket auto-retry) is requested at merge review.

## Consequences

- Hook rejections become visible, actionable task errors with a concrete fix
  instead of journal-only crash loops; the stale-`lastError` mechanism for
  this class is gone (fresh `failureReason` on every failed completion).
- Same-tree retries are bounded: one poll-cycle backoff on the runner, three
  strikes then scheduler/claim parking on the backend, operator action to
  unpark. No new task status was introduced.
- The envelope doubles as the agent handoff: failback already carries
  `gitDiagnostics` into the Tier-3 prompt, so a follow-up remediation stage
  can consume it without a new channel.

## Follow-ups (deliberately out of scope)

- Push/network/auth classification (reserved kinds, one parser).
- Team webhook on hook failure.
- Agent auto-remediation stage consuming `gitDiagnostics`.

   the process stays alive and systemd never restarts. Transient git faults
   (lock/timeout) keep the interrupt path, now carrying a reason. This
   covers task-branch (stage/merge) commits; internal `kb-recovery/*`
   snapshots bypass hooks instead (see 6).
3. **Complete-not-interrupt is the reporting vehicle.** Only the complete path
   flows through failure routing into `lastError`, timeline, history, logs,
   and the `-failure-` stage report; `interrupt()` deliberately leaves
   `lastError` alone. Worktree-setup failures report the same way — the
   complete fence only checks the claim hold, never progress state.
4. **The backend persists the envelope as `lastError.gitDiagnostics`** (new
   `hook-rejected`/`commit-failed` kinds beside `merge-conflict`/
   `sync-blocked`), classifies `failureKind: "commit-failed"` as
   non-retryable logical feedback, and parks the task after three
   consecutive same-signature strikes (`gitFailureStreak`, scheduler +
   claim skip until an operator retries, resumes, or moves).
5. **The task UI renders a dedicated callout** (hook, command, files, remedy,
   expandable full output) inside both failure banners plus a distinct card
   label — driven by the envelope shape, so backend diagnostics shapes keep
   rendering as plain text.
6. **Scoped bypass for recovery snapshots only; never bypass or auto-repair
   task output.** Internal `kb-recovery/*` snapshots bypass repo hooks via
   `commitRecoverySnapshot` (a failing hook must never strand unpushed work;
   the bypass is warn-logged with the recovery branch). Task-branch
   (stage/merge) commits never bypass — no `--no-verify` there (pinned by a
   scope test), no file deletion, no hook disabling. Parking (stop retrying)
   is the only other automation.

**Reconciliation note (2026-11-21).** This ADR originally forbade all bypass
(q6 survey override). Merged task `db49d6c6` then fixed the same incident's
recovery path with `--no-verify` recovery snapshots, and the recorded human
survey answer for q6 selects `--no-verify` retry — so this branch reconciled
onto that design during the merge with `main` (`64e428e6`): bypass is allowed
exactly inside `commitRecoverySnapshot`, forbidden everywhere else. The
`recovery` envelope phase is retained for wire compatibility but has no
producer. Human confirmation of this q6 middle ground (scoped recovery
bypass, no blanket auto-retry) is requested at merge review.

## Consequences

- Hook rejections become visible, actionable task errors with a concrete fix
  instead of journal-only crash loops; the stale-`lastError` mechanism for
  this class is gone (fresh `failureReason` on every failed completion).
- Same-tree retries are bounded: one poll-cycle backoff on the runner, three
  strikes then scheduler/claim parking on the backend, operator action to
  unpark. No new task status was introduced.
- The envelope doubles as the agent handoff: failback already carries
  `gitDiagnostics` into the Tier-3 prompt, so a follow-up remediation stage
  can consume it without a new channel.

## Follow-ups (deliberately out of scope)

- Push/network/auth classification (reserved kinds, one parser).
- Team webhook on hook failure.
- Agent auto-remediation stage consuming `gitDiagnostics`.

{"content":"# Feedback-loop retrospective — db49d6c6 (recovery `--no-verify` + dispatch containment)

Date: 2026-11-22. Case study: task `db49d6c6-bdd5-4600-aaea-15a71042ae20`
("Fix runner recovery commits failing on pre-commit hooks and crash-looping",
merged to main as `64e428e6`).

## Ticket history reviewed

- `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` + `SURVEY.md`: plan was written against unanswered
  survey questions (adopted recommendations as assumptions); answers arrived
  later and q1's answer ("skip checks for all automatic runner saves")
  conflicted with the task goal's recovery-only scope. The review stage
  adjudicated correctly (task goal authoritative) and pinned task-branch
  hook behavior with a scope test — no rework resulted, but the conflict
  cost review attention.
- `review-20261121-stage.md`: PASS with full red→green proof (449/449 runner
  tests). Two residual risks were explicitly accepted: (1) persistently
  failing tasks flap forever (interrupt/re-queue/reclaim, zero backoff);
  (2) bypassed snapshots park corrupt binaries by design.
- Git history: sibling task `1cae113f` ("Surface runner git/commit and
  pre-commit hook failures clearly in the UI", merged as `7ac148ce`) worked
  the same incident from the reporting side and needed an explicit
  reconciliation merge (`d6fa0c44`, `bb996858`) plus an ADR
  (`docs/adr/0017-commit-hook-failure-surfacing.md`) to align its original
  no-bypass stance with this ticket's scoped bypass. Its q6 survey
  originally forbade all bypass — near-miss of two concurrent tickets
  shipping contradictory designs for one incident.
- Verified on `main`: the dispatch-loop `catch` path has no backoff at all
  (only `gitFailureReported` gets one poll-cycle pause); backend 3-strikes
  parking covers only `gitFailureStreak`; the hook-bypass scope test
  (`runner/project.test.js` "allows --no-verify only inside
  commitRecoverySnapshot") pins bypass placement but not the reverse (new
  inline recovery commits would pass); no boot-id/restart-count
  crash-loop detection exists anywhere (only prose mentions).

## Agent difficulties / structural fails found

1. Containment without backoff trades a restart storm for a reclaim flap:
   a poisoned task can now pin runner capacity forever with no parking.
   Flagged as out-of-scope in the plan, accepted in review — needs its own
   ticket (created below).
2. One-directional scope test: the bypass is centralized but a future agent
   adding a third inline recovery commit gets no test failure. Cheap to
   pin (created below).
3. 10,776 silent systemd restarts: no runner restart observability
   anywhere in the stack, so the next daemon-death bug will hide the same
   way (created below).
4. Process note (no ticket — needs human judgment, not code): two
   concurrent tickets nearly shipped contradictory designs for one
   incident, and survey answers arrived after planning with one answer
   contradicting the task goal. Worth a human look at incident-linked
   ticket grouping, but not a well-specified agent ticket.

## Dedupe performed

- API base `http://localhost:3100` was unreachable (nothing listening; only
  the runner daemon runs on this host). Resolved the live backend from the
  runner env (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_BACKEND=http://192.168.1.206:3100`) and used
  it for all skill operations.
- Resolved: project `0fd41821-d8a5-4e49-bc2e-28ce8c739a0a` (kainbain),
  workflow `wf-default` (Feature Pipeline), stage `1` (Idea). Current
  executing stage is `stage-1794594754686` (retrospective) — no recursion.
- Listed all 66 tasks in `wf-default`; 13 open. None covers backoff/
  parking for generic setup failures, recovery-helper enforcement, or
  restart detection. Cross-checked git history (`--grep` for
  recover/hook/backoff/circuit/flap/crash-loop/restart) and the stale
  local task mirrors — no duplicates.

## Tickets created (3, all `execute:false`, verified in stage `1`)

1. `e3d4e9db-031c-43a9-a8e7-1e44cb1839b2` — "Back off and park assignments
   that repeatedly fail setup after containment" (generalizes the
   git-only backoff/parking to the contained-catch path).
2. `20143759-ab55-4576-be22-3e3dc44f2296` — "Pin all kb-recovery snapshot
   commits to the commitRecoverySnapshot helper" (reverse scope test +
   README rule).
3. `fd5a74bf-7f95-413c-99d6-f8a12efb489b` — "Detect and surface runner
   rapid-restart (crash-loop) storms" (boot-id heartbeats, threshold,
   degraded flag + UI banner + runbook).

Each ticket body stands alone and cites this task id as its case study.
Idempotency keys were derived as
`sha256(finding + "1" + currentTaskId)[:32]`; re-verified each ticket via
`GET /tasks/<id>?projectId=...` (all `currentStageId: 1`,
`workflowId: wf-default`, `status: waiting_human` as expected for the
human Idea stage).
